title: `glue_sql()` gives a confusing error when `.con` is missing
description:
Discovered while working on upkeep.

Calling `glue_sql()` without providing `.con` produces a cryptic error from DBI internals rather than a clear message about the missing argument:

```r
var <- "foo"
glue_sql("{var}")
#> Error: error in evaluating the argument 'conn' in selecting
#> a method for function 'dbQuoteLiteral': argument ".con" is
#> missing, with no default
```

## Expected behavior

A user-friendly error, e.g.:

```
Error in `glue_sql()`:
! `.con` is absent but must be supplied.
```

## Cause

`.con` has no default value, but because of R's lazy evaluation it isn't actually evaluated until `sql_quote_transformer()` uses it inside a call to `DBI::dbQuoteLiteral()`. By that point the error surfaces from deep inside DBI method dispatch.

The same issue applies to `glue_data_sql()`.

## Proposed fix

Force early evaluation of `.con` at the top of both `glue_sql()` and `glue_data_sql()`.

title: glue_sql only has second-resolution for timestamps in duckdb
description:
Not sure if this fits here or needs to be created at the duckdb repo.
When I use `glue_sql` with timestamps, I get different resolutions for timestamps.
For duckdb I get second-level resolution, while postgres provides a higher resolution.

I would expect to receive the sub-second resolution in both cases!

```r
glue::glue_sql(
  "INSERT INTO TEST (val) VALUES ({Sys.time()});",
  .con = DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
)
#> <SQL> INSERT INTO TEST (val) VALUES ('2025-06-20 12:20:25'::timestamp);
#                                                           ^ there is no subsecond resolution here!

glue::glue_sql(
  "INSERT INTO TEST (val) VALUES ({Sys.time()});",
  .con = DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(),
                        host = Sys.getenv("POSTGRES_HOST"),
                        port = Sys.getenv("POSTGRES_PORT"),
                        dbname = Sys.getenv("POSTGRES_DATABASE"),
                        user = Sys.getenv("POSTGRES_USER"),
                        password = Sys.getenv("POSTGRES_SECRET"))
)
#> <SQL> INSERT INTO TEST (val) VALUES ('2025-06-20 12:20:25.219384'::timestamp);
# this is what I would expect!
```

title: .null and .na arguments in glue_sql have no effect
description:
I have some code where I'm building up complex conditions to insert into a parameterized query with glue_sql. In a previous glue version, if those conditions were NULL (in R) I would insert nothing into that part of the query using `.null = DBI::SQL("")` in glue_sql. However, in 1.8.0 it appears that the .null argument no longer has any impact on the output of glue_sql, and the .na argument doesn't seem to do anything either.

Is this the intended behavior of these arguments?

``` r
library(glue)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "test.sqlite")
# In previous glue version these would be equivalent, now first returns empty query
glue_sql("select {cond}", .con = con, .null = DBI::SQL(""), cond = NULL)
#> <SQL>
glue_sql("select {cond}", .con = con, cond = DBI::SQL(""))
#> <SQL> select
# And neither .null nor .na seem to have any effect on output
glue_sql("select {cond}", .con = con, .null = "foo", .na = "foo", cond = NA)
#> <SQL> select NULL
glue_sql("select {cond}", .con = con, .null = "foo", .na = "foo", cond = NULL)
#> <SQL>
```

title: scoping for glue in multiple functions
description:
If you have one function, say a generic function that is passing glue objects, and another function that is relying on that generic function, the glue scoping is for the generic and not for where it is being used, so you have to pass the environment.

I think this is expected behavior, but it is not 100% clear to me from the documentation. [ relates to #42]

## Example where the generic `my_glue_function` is being used in `get_cat_details` but it cannot see the var `b` in scope
``` r
library(glue)

my_glue_function <- function(x, ...){
  glue(x, ...)
}

get_cat_details <- function(a){
  x <- a
  b <- nchar(x)
  my_glue_function("The cat was {x} and {b}")
}
get_cat_details("red")
#> Error:
#> ! Failed to evaluate glue component {b}
#> Caused by error:
#> ! object 'b' not found
```

<sup>Created on 2025-04-11 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

## Example where the specific function environment is passed
``` r
library(glue)

my_glue_function <- function(x, ...){
  glue(x, ...)
}
# you have to manually pass the environment 
# parent.frame default is for the outer function
get_cat_details_pass_envir <- function(a){
  x <- a
  b <- nchar(x)
  my_glue_function("The cat was {x} and {b}", .envir = environment())
}
get_cat_details_pass_envir("red")
#> The cat was red and 3
```

As for now, it seems impossible to glue a vector without concatenating the result. The output appears always to be a string of length 1.

``` r
library(tidyverse)
```

``` r
name <- "Fred"

     'my age next year is {age + 1}.')
```

title: glue_sql handling of empty vectors
description:
Post upgrade to glue version 1.7.0, we encountered a breaking change in how glue_sql handles empty vectors introduced on #292 . Previously, empty vectors were collapsed to "NULL" in SQL queries, which was functional for our use case. However, since the update, empty vectors are now collapsed to an empty string, resulting in syntax errors in SQL queries with IN clauses.

This change impacts all database queries where we dynamically generate IN clauses based on possibly empty vectors. The new behavior leads to malformed SQL queries and runtime errors, significantly affecting our data retrieval processes.

Could we consider reintroducing the previous behavior of collapsing empty vectors to "NULL" in SQL queries, or provide an option to toggle between the two behaviors? This would allow for backward compatibility and flexibility for different use cases.

We've implemented a workaround where we manually check for empty vectors and adjust the SQL query accordingly. However, this adds complexity and boilerplate code, which was elegantly handled by glue_sql in previous versions.

title: glue_sql converts length-0 vectors to NULL in asterisk-expansion
description:
```R
x <- character(0)
glue::glue_sql("{x*}")
# <SQL> NULL
```
When used as part of an SQL expression, this can happen:
```R
glue::glue_sql("select foo from bar where baz in ({x*})")
# <SQL> select foo from bar where baz in (NULL)
```
... which has different semantics (in most SQL variants) than what I believe most users likely are intending when `x` is empty:
```R
# <SQL> select foo from bar where baz in ()  <-- the _intended_ SQL, I think.
```

I've confirmed this also happens with DB object identified expansion, too, i.e.:
```R
"{`x`*}"
# <SQL> NULL
```

title: Consider using doubling for escaping in `.literal = TRUE`
description:
I am wondering if `.literal = TRUE` should still allow double delimiters for escaping. I.e. this currently fails:
```r
❯ glue::glue("{'{'}", .literal = TRUE)
Error in glue_data(.x = NULL, ..., .sep = .sep, .envir = .envir, .open = .open,  :
  Expecting '}'
```
and AFAICT there is no easy way of writing a (non well formed) literal brace in a glue string, apart from using substitution:
```r
❯ glue::glue("{'{{'}", .literal = TRUE)
Error in glue_data(.x = NULL, ..., .sep = .sep, .envir = .envir, .open = .open,  :
  Expecting '}'
```

As you might suspect this affects cli, because cli uses doubling as escaping currently, so it cannot switch to `.literal = TRUE`. On the other hand `.literal = TRUE` would be much better for the cases when people include literal quotes in the string, e.g. https://github.com/r-lib/cli/issues/370

If doubling is still accepted for escaping, then `.literal = TRUE` does not break cli, and I think it is also beneficial in general to be able to escape the delimiter.

title: `glue_sql` struggles with Inf, -Inf, and NaN
description:
Probably related (at least in spirit) to r-dbi/DBI#361.

Different DB back-ends will certainly have different behavior here, making this tricky. PostgreSQL (as the example with which I'm most familiar) supports `'Infinity'`, `'-Infinity'`, and `'NaN'` as numeric values (quotes necessary), as documented [here](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-numeric.html). (Note that in earlier versions of PostgreSQL, the acceptable list of strings was smaller ... [here's the documentation for v8.2](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/8.2/datatype-numeric.html) -- the oldest still-supported version).

With a PostgreSQL DBI connection object, here's how these values are converted:
```r
glue::glue_sql("select x from y where z > {Inf}+ {-Inf} + {NaN}", .con = conn)
```
```
<SQL> select x from y where z > Inf + -Inf + NULL
```
... which will (syntax) err.

If adding some explicit type-casting to be a bit safer, we get:
```r
glue::glue_sql("select x from y where z > {Inf}::float8 + {-Inf}::float8 + {NaN}::float8", .con = conn)
```
```
<SQL> select x from y where z > Inf::float8 + -Inf::float8 + NULL::float8
```
... which unfortunately will:
1. still (syntax) err on the infinite values, **and**
2. logically err on `NULL` value (as `NULL` math is different from `NaN` math, at least with PostgreSQL).

I'm not 100% sure what exactly should be done here, but I didn't see any issue mentioning this so minimally I figured I'd open this for discussion and future reference about this scenario. I believe this scenario arises in a fair number of instances, a common one being something like: `"select x from y where {max(z)} > z"` and `z` happens to be zero-length in the calling R code. Obviously the caller can try to conditionally rewrite that predicate, but it's pretty easy to see how this sneaks into code (and I'd argue having alternate SQL interpolations in application code for boundary conditions adds much cruff at the wrong level :-)).

title: FR: Error handling when variable is not found: specific error message and class
description:
When using an unknown variable in `glue()`, the error message can be a little cryptic:

``` r
library(glue)
x=5
glue("x={x}")
#> x=5
glue("w={w}")
#> Error in eval(parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE), envir): object 'w' not found
```
<sup>Created on 2021-10-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

This is most true when `glue()` is used within a package and even more if the pattern is provided by the package user.   
A specific message, such as "Could not find variable 'w' when glueing '{pattern}'", would make it much clearer.

Moreover, as read in the book ["Advanced R"](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/conditions.html#custom-conditions):

> One of the challenges of error handling in R is that most functions generate one of the built-in conditions, which contain only a `message` and a `call`. That means that if you want to detect a specific type of error, you can only work with the text of the error message. This is error-prone, not only because the message might change over time, but also because messages can be translated into other languages.

Indeed, dealing with user-defined patterns in glue throwing this error would be a million times easier if this error had a specific error subclass that you would be able to check, as `rlang::abort(.subclass=)` would do.

Would this be an acceptable feature request?

title: Tidyverse consistency
description:
``` r
library(stringr)

str_c(1:2, "-", character())
#> Error in `stop_vctrs()`: Can't recycle `..1` (size 2) to match `..3` (size 0).
str_glue("{x}-{y}", x = 1:2, y = character())

str_c("-", c(1, NA), "-")
#> [1] "-1-" NA
str_glue("-{x}-", x = c(1, NA))
#> -1-
#> -NA-

str_glue("-{x}-", x = NULL)
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

Three problems:

* Need to error if vector lengths are inconsistent
* `NA` should be infectious
* `NULL` should be silently dropped (not treated like `character()`)

The last two can already be control via arguments:

``` r
library(stringr)
str_glue("-{x}-", x = c(1, NA), .na = NULL)
#> -1-
#> NA
str_c("-", NULL, "-", .null = NULL)
#> [1] "--"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

But I think it would be good to consider a path forward to bring the defaults into alignment with the rest of the tidyverse, even if it has to go via some sort of edition.

title: Add explicit handling for length 0 variables in glue
description:
Currently, the glue function returns character(0) when one of the variables to be evaluated has length 0 and is not NULL. The NULL case is already handled by the .null parameter. However, the behaviour with length 0 objects can be confusing and potentially lead to unintended consequences.

I propose adding a new feature that properly handles length 0 variables in the glue function. This feature should provide a clear and consistent behaviour for dealing with length 0 objects, making it easier for users to understand and work with the output in such cases.

I have already implemented a working solution with test cases using an additional parameter, analogous to .null.  I would like to contribute it to the tidyverse/glue package. Before creating a pull request, I wanted to open an issue to discuss the potential changes, gather feedback, and ensure that the new feature aligns with the project's goals and guidelines.

Please let me know your thoughts on this proposed feature, and if it's something you'd be interested in incorporating into the tidyverse/glue package.

##### Current implementation:
```r
n1 <- "foo"
n2 <- character()
res <- glue::glue("{n1} and {n2} go together")
print(res)
#Output: character(0)
```

##### Suggested implementation:
```r
n1 <- "foo"
n2 <- character()
res <- glue::glue("{n1} and {n2} go together", .empty = "bar")
print(res)
#Output: "foo and bar go together"
```

local(glue(x), envir = e)
# Fails:
local(lapply(x, glue), envir = e)

This behaviour also causes `lapply(x, glue)` to fail in a RMarkdown document.

title: glue_[data]_sql's asterisk notation fails on an SQL vector
description:
`glue_sql`'s asterisk notation is very useful for concatenating a vector into a comma-separated list. However, it doesn't seem to work when the vector contains DBI::SQL elements.

See the MWE below*:

```r
library(DBI)

packageVersion("glue")
#> ‘1.4.1’

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")

a <- letters[1:3]
glue::glue_sql("{a*}", .con = con)
#> <SQL> 'a', 'b', 'c'

a <- SQL(letters[1:3])
glue::glue_sql("{a*}", .con = con)
#> <SQL> a
#> <SQL> b
#> <SQL> c
```

Looking into the `glue` source code, the problem seems to be in the definition of `glue:::sql_quote_transformer` (trimming the irrelevant portions):

```
function (connection, .na) 
{
    # [...]
    function(text, envir) {
        should_collapse <- grepl("[*]$", text)
        if (should_collapse) {
            # [...]
        }
        m <- gregexpr("^`|`$", text)
        is_quoted <- any(m[[1]] != -1)
        if (is_quoted) {
            # [...]
        }
        else {
            res <- eval(parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE), 
                envir)
            if (inherits(res, "SQL")) {
                return(res)
            }
           # [...]
        }
        if (should_collapse) {
            res <- glue_collapse(res, ", ")
        }
        # [...]
        res
    }
}
```

Specifically, both cases get `should_collapse = TRUE` and `is_quoted = FALSE`. However, the `else` section of the `if (is_quoted)` block contains a check for whether the contents inherit from SQL, in which case they are immediately returned, before the collapse is actually performed at the end of the function.

If of interest, this situation arose because I was trying to write the following statement:

```SQL
UPDATE f
SET a = 0
FROM foo f
INNER JOIN (VALUES {values*})
            v(id, a)
  ON  f.Id = v.Id
```

where `{values}*` contains the vector of results from a previous `glue` statement built from a dataframe (`oldFoo`):

```r
values <- glue::glue_data_sql(
        "({id}, {a})",
        .x = oldFoo,
        .con = con)
```

Since `{id}` and `{a}` don't have an asterisk, this converts `oldFoo` into a vector of SQL strings, which I'd then hoped to collapse into a comma-separated list as expected by the `VALUES` SQL statement.

Interestingly, this problem didn't exist in previous versions of `glue`: [this online compiler](https://rextester.com/ZIJTW78734) uses glue 1.2.0 and it works. Looking at `glue:::sql_quote_transformer`'s source code on that version, we see it was different and didn't include the "if SQL then return" block.

---

\* To be perfectly transparent, the MWE above contains a lie: my actual case uses a `pool` object pointing to an SQL Server database, not an SQLite connection. But this would seem irrelevant to the matter at hand.

title: all output lost when using if statement without else in glue
description:
Hi,
    I was using an if statement in glue, and ran across something that I think this is not the intended behavior?

If I use an if statement without specifying the else (FALSE) condition, all output is lost. I am not sure if this is a bug, but it was not the behavior I was expecting. In the case that the else statement is not specified, it doesn't matter what is present in any other number of glue() statement, the combined glue string is empty.

I expected that the glue string when no else case was specified would return an empty string, and let me combine multiple if statements in sequence, without specifying the else. 

Thanks!

```r
## This fails
test1 = FALSE
stuff1 = glue("Hello")
thing1 = glue("{if(test1) \" you\" }")

stuff1+thing1 ## nothing is printed - any glue statements combined are lost

## This works
test2 = TRUE
stuff2 = glue("Hello")
thing2 = glue("{if(test2) \" you\" }") ## these work

stuff2+thing2

##This works when test is FALSE
test3 = FALSE
stuff3 = glue("Hello")
thing3 = glue("{if(test3) \" you\" else \" me\"}") ## this properly combines the statement

stuff3+thing3

## Combination of anything with the open ended if statement also results in a fail
```

title: Unexpected behavior when passing the dots to a wrapper of `glue_sql()`
description:
I made a wrapper to more easily create my queries and found an unexpected behaviour in `glue_sql()`. These are minimal examples of the problem. The wrapper passes a character vector and named arguments to the `...` argument of `glue_sql()` after a connection to take advantage of the SQL quoting and to avoid typing.

``` r
make_query <- function(...) {
    con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite())
    query <- glue::glue_sql(..., .con = con)
    DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
    return(query)
}
```

When used directly, it behaves as expected.

```r
make_query("SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = {id}", id = "007")
#> <SQL> SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = '007'
```

However, wrapping this function makes sense for easily making more specific queries. Let's say I want the data from an id:

```r
specific_query <- function(id) {
    query <- "SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = {id}"
    make_query(query, id = id)
}
```
But this raises the following error:
```r
specific_query("007")
#> Error in eval(parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE), envir): object 'id' not found
```
I'm not sure what is happening here. The error message makes me think that  `glue_sql()` receives `query` but not `id = id`. However, the function documentation says:

> ...	[expressions]
Unnamed arguments are taken to be expression string(s) to format. Multiple inputs are concatenated together before formatting. Named arguments are taken to be temporary variables available for substitution.

Which makes me think that `make_query(query, id = id)` may be treating `query` as a named argument, leaving no strings to format for `glue_sql()`. ¿Or maybe the problem is the `.con` argument?

## Workaround

I  get the expected output when instead of passing directly to `glue_sql()` I list the dots contents and use `do.call()` with them. So, I found a solution, yes. But I report this because I know why this one works, but I don't know why just passing the dots doesn't.

```r
make_query2 <- function(...) {
    con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite())
    dots <- list(...)
    dots$`.con` <- con
    query <- do.call(glue::glue_sql, dots)
    DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
    return(query)
}

make_query2("SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = {id}", id = "007")
#> <SQL> SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = '007'

specific_query2 <- function(id) {
    query <- "SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = {id}"
    make_query2(query, id = id)
}

specific_query2("007")
#> <SQL> SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = '007'
```

title: Feature request: print nicely formatted data frames
description:
When I try to format a `data.frame` the result is quite weird:

```r
glue("Here are two cars:\n {mtcars[1:2,]}")
```

This gives the following output:

```
Here are two cars:
c(21, 21)
Here are two cars:
c(6, 6)
Here are two cars:
c(160, 160)
Here are two cars:
c(110, 110)
[...some more similar lines...]
```

I wrote the the following helper function / workaround:

```r
format_df <- function(df) {
  paste0(capture.output(df), collapse="\n")
}

glue("Here are two cars:\n {format_df(mtcars[1:2,])}")
```

This gives the intended output:

```
Here are two cars:
              mpg cyl disp  hp drat    wt  qsec vs am gear carb
Mazda RX4      21   6  160 110  3.9 2.620 16.46  0  1    4    4
Mazda RX4 Wag  21   6  160 110  3.9 2.875 17.02  0  1    4    4
```

I think this could be pretty easy integrated in `glue`: For each variable where `is.data.frame` is true, such a helper function is called to transform the data.frame to a multiline string.

Would this be a feature of interest for the `glue` library?

title: waldo version requirement for tests
description:
I know it's not a strict requirement to have version requirements for Suggested packages, but it took me quite a while to figure this out, so I figure I'd flag it.

I'm trying to update glue from 1.4.2 --> 1.6.0.

It appears `waldo` needs to be of a certain version for this to work. Otherwise we get a pile of test failures like:

```
── Failure (Line 7): glue and glue_data safe do not execute code ─────────────────────
glue("{1 + 1}") (`actual`) not equal to "2" (`expected`).

`actual` is an S3 object of class <glue/character>, a character vector
`expected` is a character vector ('2')

── Failure (Line 8): glue and glue_data safe do not execute code ─────────────────────
glue_safe("{1 + 1}") (`actual`) not equal to "5" (`expected`).

`actual` is an S3 object of class <glue/character>, a character vector
`expected` is a character vector ('5')
```

Luckily I'm familiar enough with `testthat`/`waldo` internals to recognize the issue from the error message -- `waldo::compare()` sees the classes differ on the objects; what we need is `waldo::compare_proxy()` to have a `glue` method that ignores the `glue` class. But I see a `compare_proxy.glue` method in R/utils.R -- why isn't it taking hold?

The issue appears to be that `compare_proxy()` is never called.

The issue resolves when I update waldo 0.2.5 --> 0.3.1 simultaneously.

I can't tell from reading `waldo`'s NEWS what made the change (looks like 0.3.0 is likely?), nor do I have any easy way to check manually.

title: Bug: `glue` gobbles up first few characters if string starts with an actual newline followed by `⎵⎵\n`
description:
Here's a reprex:

``` r
packageVersion("glue")
#> [1] '1.5.0'

a <- 1
b <- "A"
glue::glue("
  \n  SUM(IIF(a = {a}, a, NULL)) AS {b}")
#>   
#> M(IIF(a = 1, a, NULL)) AS A          # <---- SUM(...) became M(...)
glue::glue("
  SUM(IIF(a = {a}, a, NULL)) AS {b}")
#> SUM(IIF(a = 1, a, NULL)) AS A
glue::glue("
\n  SUM(IIF(a = {a}, a, NULL)) AS {b}")
#> 
#> SUM(IIF(a = 1, a, NULL)) AS A
glue::glue("  \n  SUM(IIF(a = {a}, a, NULL)) AS {b}")
#> SUM(IIF(a = 1, a, NULL)) AS A
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-22 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>


Note that the strings are identical except the first starts with a newline followed by `⎵⎵\n` (two spaces and a newline character), and therefore its `SUM(...)` becomes `M(...)`.

Removing either the spaces and/or the `\n` solves the problem, as does removing the initial newline.

This likely has to do with the trimming rules (see `trim()`), but I thought this format would pass muster. The rules as defined in the `trim()` man-page are:

> - Leading and trailing whitespace from the first and last lines is removed.
> - A uniform amount of indentation is stripped from the second line on, equal to the minimum indentation of all non-blank lines after the first.
> - Lines can be continued across newlines by using \\\\.

For this case:

- By the first rule, the empty first line is dropped.
- The second rule should remove two indents from each of the other two lines (the first originally containing the two spaces before the `\n`, the other everything after it, including its two initial spaces).
- The third rule is irrelevant.

So the second rule would indicate that the `  SUM(...)` line should have its two leading spaces dropped, but in fact four characters are dropped (the two spaces and `SU`).

title: Allow hashtags in single-line input strings
description:
I've been playing with something akin to the [collapse_transformer()](https://glue.tidyverse.org/articles/transformers.html#collapse-transformer) example, but I'd like to be able to include `#` in one-line input strings.

What I want to do is essentially the following, where I would parse the template string in the transformer, but unfortunately it doesn't make it [past the parser](https://github.com/tidyverse/glue/blob/a3375fe0c8ba6b3f160e4774d6b4ad883944b6fb/src/glue.c#L112-L117).

``` r
glue::glue("{#b a}")
# no output due to #b
```

Here are a few examples using an identity transformer that just returns the text that reaches the transformer.

``` r
identity <- function(x, ...) x

glue::glue("{a}", .transformer = identity)
#> a
```

`"{a*}"` works and the transformer receives `"a*"`, but `"{a#}"` does not work: the transformer isn’t called …

``` r
glue::glue("{a*}", .transformer = identity)
#> a*
glue::glue("{a#}", .transformer = identity)
```

…unless the `#` is followed by a new line.

``` r
glue::glue("{a#\n}", .transformer = identity)
#> a#
```

Another example without the identity transformer.

``` r
a <- "apple"
glue::glue("{a#}")
glue::glue("{a#\n}")
#> apple
```

I can see where problems could arise with incomplete expressions due to comments, but it also makes sense that such problems would throw parsing errors.

``` r
glue::glue("{c(a,#\na)}")
#> apple
#> apple
glue::glue("{c(a,#a)}")
glue::glue("{c(a,#a)\n}")
#> Error in parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE): <text>:3:0: unexpected end of input
#> 1: c(a,#a)
#> 2: 
#>   ^
```

That said, one place where changing the parser might break current behavior is that currently empty expressions cause the entire result to be zero-length. Except for the last, the following all return `character(0)`.

``` r
glue::glue("{#a} {'banana'}")
glue::glue("{#a\n} {'banana'}")
glue::glue("{a#a} {'banana'}")
glue::glue("{a#a\n} {'banana'}")
#> apple banana
```

title: glue_sql should allow whitespace between asterisk and closing bracket
description:
I often write long SQL queries with some parameters spread throughout. This is handled beautifully by `glue_sql`, especially due to its asterisk operator which allows us to transform vectors into comma-separated lists.

However, glue's benefit of allowing code and string constants to be elegantly blended can also be a bit of a downside when dealing with large queries, since it becomes hard to tell at a glance what is a parameter (a single word surrounded by brackets vanishes when in the middle of a query with a dozen joins.

The inelegance (not to mention security risks) of using `paste()` at least has the benefit of making it painfully clear what is constant and what is variable, especially in an IDE like RStudio with different color-coding for strings and variables.

Something I've found helpful is adding spaces between the word and the brackets: `WHERE x = { x }` instead of `WHERE x = {x}`. This was inspired by the tidyverse style guide's recommended practice for the embracing operator `{{ x }}`.

However, this doesn't work neatly with the asterisk operator:

``` r
x <- 1:3
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")

glue::glue_sql(.con = con, "{ x* }")
#> Error in parse(text = text, keep.source = FALSE): <text>:2:0: unexpected end of input
#> 1:  x* 
#>    ^
glue::glue_sql(.con = con, "{ x *}")
#> <SQL> 1, 2, 3
```

<sup>Created on 2021-05-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

The asterisk must be the character immediately preceding the closing bracket. But I'd argue that `{ x* }` is more natural than `{ x *}`.

At a glance, this could be solved with a small change to `glue:::sql_quote_transformer`, which includes the following test:

```r
should_collapse <- grepl("[*]$", text)
```

This could be trivially modified into

```r
should_collapse <- grepl("[*] *$", text)
```
thereby allowing any number of trailing spaces. (Maybe even use `\w` to allow any sort of white space?)

I'm no expert in regex performance, but I'm guessing this would come at almost no performance cost.

title: String comparison method (compare.glue) doesn't work with testthat 3rd edition
description:
I was just setting up tests in a new project using [testthat 3e](https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/third-edition.html) and found that comparing a string made using glue doesn't match an equivalent character string.

The change in testthat to using waldo::compare means that [the compare.glue method](https://github.com/tidyverse/glue/blob/f0a7b2a21162980c153edd68a9f5d279af1d426b/R/utils.R#L74-L80) isn't called.

Here's a reprex demonstrating the difference between testthat 2e and 3e:

``` r
library(glue)
library(testthat)

a <- glue("this is a test string")
b <- "this is a test string"

test_that("glue and character strings match - testthat 2e", {
  local_edition(2)
  expect_equal(a, b)
})
#> Test passed 🎊

test_that("glue and character strings match - testthat 3e", {
  local_edition(3)
  expect_equal(a, b)
})
#> ── Failure (<text>:14:3): glue and character strings match - testthat 3e ───────
#> `a` (`actual`) not equal to `b` (`expected`).
#> 
#> `actual` is an S3 object of class <glue/character>, a character vector
#> `expected` is a character vector ('this is a test string')

testthat::compare(a, b)
#> Equal
waldo::compare(a, b)
#> `old` is an S3 object of class <glue/character>, a character vector
#> `new` is a character vector ('this is a test string')
```

<sup>Created on 2021-02-24 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0)</sup>

Workarounds for now would be to use testthat 2e (remove/omit the `Config/testthat/edition: 3` line from `DESCRIPTION` in projects using testthat >= 3.0.0), or wrap the expected values in tests where glue creates the actual string(s) with `as_glue()`.

But it looks like [compare_proxy](https://waldo.r-lib.org/reference/compare_proxy.html) provides a way to override the default comparison behaviour in waldo. I'd be happy to put together a pull request if it's wanted. Thanks.

title: Shorthand for coercing glue(...) to character (e.g. for if_else or case_when)
description:
I often find myself using `glue(...)` within `if_else` or `case_when`, mixed with simple strings. In order for this to work I have to explicitly coerce the glue object to character (or the strings to glue). It would be very convenient if there were a shorthand, e.g. `glue_chr(...)` which automatically returned the result as a pure character class.


```r
d <- tibble(x = 1:10)

mutate(d, y = case_when(
    x <= 3 ~ "x <= 3", 
    x >= 8, "x >= 8",
    TRUE ~ glue("x = {x}") %>% as.character
))

# With shorthand
# ... TRUE ~ glue_chr("x = {x}") ...
```

Unfortunately, defining a utility function naively didn't work because of the environment.
```r
# This function will not work in the use case above, error: "object 'x' not found"
glue_chr <- function(...) as.character(glue(...))
```

title: glue_sql: Weird quoting issue with embedded function
description:
I face a weird quoting issue.

Here is the circumstance:
I have a function `sq2_tblful` that returns the fully qualified PostgreSQL name of a table by its name; by example:

```R
oriidt <- "tbl"
tbl <- sq2_tblful(oriidt)
```

`tbl` is now equal to `"rnk"."tbl"` (I am using `DBI::Id` to get the fully qualified name as per your previous recommendation).

Now, as allowed (?), I insert the function `sq2_tblful` into a SQL expression, thus:
```R
thesql <- glue_sql("SELECT pst_formula AS tno FROM {`sq2_tblful(tblidt)`} WHERE nam='{`oriidt`}';", .con=cnx)
```
The rationale is that I want to avoid any variable and have a compact, self-sufficient, executable expression I can execute from R using `glue_sql`.

The embedded function is well understood but I get the following SQL expression, which yields a wrong result because of the double quoting of `'"ppl"'`:
```SQL
SELECT pst_formula AS tno FROM "rnk"."tbl" WHERE nam='"ppl"';
```
The correct SQL expression should be:
```SQL
SELECT pst_formula AS tno FROM "rnk"."tbl" WHERE nam='ppl';
```

Please help.

Stephen

title: Better handling of empty subqueries in glue_sql
description:
I am very pleased with the modularity allowed by `glue_sql` when writing SQL queries, more specifically **PostgreSQL** queries.
There is a case that could be better covered though: when a subquery is optional and therefore sometimes **empty**.
In that case, `glue_sql` returns an empty string between single quotes instead of returning a space/empty string, which, IMO, would be preferable.

```R
oriidt <- "thetable"
orisch <- "theschema"
sqladd <- "" # the additional query here is empty but could be an addition to the query within WHERE() 
thesql <- glue_sql("UPDATE {`orisch`}.{`oriidt`} AS OUT SET act_key = '4' WHERE ({sqlsub}) > 1 {sqladd};", .con=cnx)
DBI::dbExecute(cnx, thesql)
```
thesql as returned by glue_sql is:
```R
<SQL> UPDATE "poi"."plc"AS OUT SET act_key = '4' WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "poi"."plc" AS INR WHERE INR."nam" = OUT."nam ' ') > 1;
```
The single quotes at the very end prevent the query to be executed.

title: Better handing of Schemas of PostgreSQL in glue_sql
description:
When using `DBI::dbExecute()` and `glue` and a PostgreSQL database I can write the schema before the table, separated by a dot, thus:
```R
oritbl <- "theschema.thetable"
thesql <- glue("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {`oritbl`}")
DBI::dbExecute(cnx, thesql)
```
now `thesql` is equal to:
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM theschema.thetable`
as was expected.

But when I use `glue_sql` instead of `glue`, `thesql` is equal to:
`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "theschema"."thetable"`
which is **not executable** because of the double quotes around `"theschema"`.

Could you detect the presence of a schema before the table name and not quote it?

title: Expose .transformer argument in glue_[data_]sql() and export sql_quote_transformer
description:
Is there a particular reason why the `.transformer()` argument isn't made available in `glue_sql` and `glue_data_sql`?

I was hoping to create my own transformer to compose with `sql_quote_transformer` which adds a suffix `-` (i.e. `{foo-}`) which indicates the contents of `foo` should be evaluated raw, without escaping.

This can be very unsafe, of course, but it'd sometimes be useful when dynamically building the SQL string from safe chunks.

I currently do this by wrapping the relevant strings with `DBI::SQL`, which works fine, but having a raw transformer with the `{foo-}` shorthand would be nice.

However, since the .transformer argument isn't exposed, this can't be done. And, actually, even if it were exposed, I wouldn't be able to compose my transformer with the `sql_quote_transformer` because it currently isn't exported.

So the only way I could do this would be by copying the current implementation of `glue_sql` and the `sql_quote_transformer` and hope they're never modified.

So, is there a reason why the `.transformer` isn't exposed and/or why the `sql_quote_transformer` isn't exported? The other solution would be doing the transformer composition internally, but I wouldn't know how to do that without adding a dependency to `purrr::compose`, which goes against the "small, fast, dependency free" philosophy of `glue`.

title: Feature request: syntax highlighting with Glue
description:
I much prefer using glue over paste0 and other equivalent solutions. One of the main criticisms that I've heard, however, is that glue doesn't support syntax highlighting within strings and interpolations can be easily lost in a large string. In this case, there is R code that outputs SQL scripts and glue makes it much easier to see what the final SQL script will actually look like over paste0, but there isn't syntax highlighting to differentiate interpolations from the rest of the string.

I wanted to 1) call that out as an issue that some people have with it's current implementation and 2) ask if there are patterns that would help these people adopt glue by giving them syntax highlighting ~somehow~

title: Should glue strings print with a header?
description:
Perhaps glue strings should print with a header so they are not confused with code:

```r
foo <- "x"
bar <- "y"
glue::glue("{foo} ~ {bar}")
#> x ~ y

x ~ y
#> x ~ y
```

With the header it'd look like:

```r
glue::glue("{foo} ~ {bar}")
#> <glue>
#> x ~ y
```

Another solution is to keep R's string representation, which would be more consistent with base strings. The downside is that the output would be heavier when the string contains formatting characters:

```r
glue("x ~ y")
#> <glue>
#> "x ~ y"

glue("x\ny")
#> <glue>
#> "x\ny"
#> -- Output --
#> x
#> y
```

title: trim() mishandles indentation-only lines shorter than min_indent
description:
`trim()` calculates the "minimum indent" of every line after the first, and then removes that number of characters from the beginning of every line after the first. I encountered this while working on the related #162.

`min_indent` is calculated by a routine that ignores indentation (spaces and tabs) on blank lines - lines containing only indentation. Consequently, the newline that terminates these lines can get trimmed, which causes the following line to include spurious leading whitespace.

Failing example:

```r
library(glue)
library(testthat)
expect_identical(
  trim("
       \ta
       \tb
      \t
       \tc"),
  "a\nb\n\nc"
)
```

In the character vector passed to `trim()`, the penultimate line contains only indentation (6 spaces followed by a tab).

When `trim()` is copying parts of the old string to a new one, it skips over the newline that delimits the penultimate and last lines, and the whitespace from the penultimate line is included in the last line.

title: Mixing glue with "character" class
description:
I love how readable `glue()` code is, but I refrain from using it in two cases: (a) when I want to minimize dependencies and (b) when mixed with regular "character"s.  

A [previous issue](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/3478) touched on (b), and I was hoping it could be revisited.  

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(glue)

x <- "bar"

case_when(
  x == "foo" ~ "x is foo",
  TRUE ~ sprintf("x is %s!", x)
)
#> [1] "x is bar!"

case_when(
  x == "foo" ~ "x is foo",
  TRUE ~ glue("x is {x}!")
)
#> must have class `character`, not class `glue/character`

case_when(
  x == "foo" ~ glue("x is foo"),
  TRUE ~ glue("x is {x}!")
)
#> x is bar!
```

<sup>Created on 2019-12-22 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

I would love for the middle case to work, especially since `glue()` _seems_ like it should be compatible with the outputs of `paste()` and `sprintf()`, and with character types in general.  I can think of two possible solutions:

* loosen the requirements in `dplyr:::check_class()` (specifically: `identical(class(x), class(template))`) to match any classes
* create a version of glue that outputs type "character" only

Thoughts?  Happy to contribute to the change if it helps!

```r
#' @param . single value coerceed to a character 
#' 
#' @details 
#' 
#' `glue_this` is a short-cut for piping a single value into `...` expressions. 
#' The single value is assigned to `.` and can be interpolated in the expression(s)
#' using `{.}`  
#' 
#' @examples 
#' 
#'   "Fred" %>% glue_this('This is {.}; Say "Hi" to {.}!')   # This is Fred; Say "Hi" to Fred!     
#'   
#' @export   
  
glue_this <- function( ., ..., .open = "{", .close = "}" ) { 
  env <- as.environment( list(. = .) )
  glue::glue( ..., .envir=as.environment( list( . = as.character(.) )), .open=.open, .close=.close )
}
```

title: Formatters
description:
Are there any plans of adding formatters?

To clarify, by “formatter” I mean (1) an interface and (2) a glue syntax that advanced formatting of glue tokens. Here’s an example:

```r
glue('π = {pi}')
glue('π to two decimal places = {format(pi, digits = 3)}')
```

With formatters, the second line could be for instance written as

```r
glue('π to two decimal places = {pi:0.2}')
```

Many libraries offer similar capabilities, for instance [composite formatting in .NET](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/composite-formatting).

Ideally this would be extensible, allowing users to register their own formatters. For instance the following is thinkable:

```r
arrgh_glue = function (str, options) {
    gsub('r', 'R', str)
}

# optionally, though ideally not necessary:
#   register_glue_formatter(arrgh = arrgh_glue)

name = 'Konrad'
glue('Hello, {name:arrgh}!')
# Hello, KonRad!
```

[The .NET documentation has some more examples](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/system.string.format(v=vs.110).aspx#Format6_Example) that show the scope of what could be possible.

title: Suppress NAs in `glue::glue()`?

```R
#> [1] "809.io"  "NA.io"   "help.io"
```

```R
glue::glue("{sv}.io")
#> 809.io
```

`stringr::str_c` performs better:

```R
stringr::str_c(sv, ".io")
```

A few years ago I asked this question on SO

The problem is summarised as follows: given 1) a template string, 2) a named list of values, insert those values in the template (with evaluation of R code), but return an error if one or more named values are missing. The solutions with brew or whisker were not particularly elegant. 

I think glue provides a good alternative, but it would be nice to have a helper function that automatically enables checking of absent values in the environment (and get their name in the error message).

```
library(glue)

# Hello Chris You have just won $124!
```

title: glue_data() ignores .envir when .x is an environment
description:
When the `.x` argument of `glue_data()` is an environment, the evaluation of `...` takes place in `.x` and not in `.envir`, contrary to the documented role of `.envir`. In particular, if `...` is not in `.x`, then `glue_data()` will fail.

Is this the intended behavior?

Example:
```R
env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
env$a <- "This is 'a'"

text <- "{a}"

glue_data(.x = env, text)
## Error in eval(x, envir = data, enclos = envir) : object 'text' not found
```
`glue_data()` has not evaluated `text` in `.envir = parent.frame()`.

Naively, I would expect `.x` to be used solely for object look-up, i.e., as if `.x` were coerced to a list:
```R
glue_data(.x = as.list(env), text)
## This is 'a'
```
